title.quote: Understanding and Meeting Practitioner Needs When Measuring Representational Harms Caused by LLM-Based Systems
title.justification: Title as given at the top of the paper.
title.value: Understanding and Meeting Practitioner Needs When Measuring Representational Harms Caused by LLM-Based Systems

extractions.description: A qualitative interview study (12 semi-structured interviews with practitioners who evaluate LLM-based systems) plus a PRISMA-guided systematic literature review, examining whether publicly available instruments for measuring representational harms meet practitioner needs, and offering recommendations grounded in measurement theory and pragmatic measurement. No models were trained or executed.

type.quote: Via semi-structured interviews with 12 such practitioners, we find that practitioners are often unable to use publicly available instruments for measuring representational harms.
type.justification: The paper reports an empirical qualitative study based on interviews and thematic analysis, though it involves no computational experiments.

name.quote: The NLP research community has made publicly available numerous instruments for measuring representational harms caused by large language model (LLM)-based systems.
name.justification: The paper addresses the NLP research community and its measurement instruments.

name.quote: As studies examining the uptake of other responsible AI artifacts have found, practitioner needs as assumed in the research literature are often different from those actually voiced by practitioners
name.justification: The paper studies responsible AI artifacts and harm measurement practice.

name.quote: We build on prior work from HCI showing that practitioners often struggle to use artifacts developed by researchers
name.justification: The study builds on and uses HCI interview-study methodology.

name.quote: Drawing on measurement theory and pragmatic measurement, we provide recommendations for addressing these challenges
name.justification: The paper draws on measurement theory from the social sciences.
